# Quality and evidence

`tools/quality/definitions.ts` is the check-ID/requirement/command source. `pnpm check` runs project-local Vite+ formatting, lint and strict type checking once, plus runtime boundaries, dependencies and documentation, including standard skill YAML name/description and directory identity. Root options are common; package Vite configs own runtime/test/build only. SDK runtime types and generated route trees are excluded from formatting/lint, not silently substituted for source checks.

`pnpm test` runs tooling and package unit/contract tests. `pnpm gate:pre-pr -- --base <sha>` selects changed packages and reverse dependencies using real manifests. Runtime configuration/lock changes and an unknown base select every application; documentation, isolated tooling tests and CI-selection/security plumbing receive global checks without application execution. Blueprint changes select their owning packages and consumers. `pnpm gate:full` explicitly runs the complete selected configuration: builds, real Worker tests, development and production browser/a11y/VRT, [all-100 Lighthouse](lighthouse.md) and native tests. Static checking remains global because it is lightweight. Missing scripts, no tests, failures and timeout fail. A nonselected package is `not_required` with a graph reason; blocked checks never count as passed.

## CI selection

Normal PR and main-push runs use the committed diff and manifest reverse dependencies, not an unconditional full suite. The plan in `artifacts/ci-plan.json` is the single job/matrix decision. PR comparison is against the latest base; push comparison is against the previous main commit. It does not substitute an unchecked previous PR head or an older green report. A broad integration PR can therefore still require the complete suite.

Reference sync also updates `.template.json` ownership hashes. The planner and local gate verify each changed hash against the actual changed file and ignore only that bookkeeping delta. Changes to options, package selection, version or lock metadata, missing state and unverifiable hashes retain broad validation. Both the raw and execution diffs remain in the CI plan for review.

| Changed responsibility                                                        | Required work beyond global static/tooling checks                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| README, docs, skill instructions, isolated tooling tests or CI-selection code | No application/native/generated/O11y jobs                                                                                              |
| Application implementation                                                    | Changed application and reverse consumers; Windows Worker when Workers are affected; all three actual OS jobs when Desktop is affected |
| One application blueprint                                                     | Only generated configurations containing that application; unrelated Desktop uses renderer validation                                  |
| Shared contract/UI                                                            | Manifest consumers; a shared blueprint also selects its generated consumers                                                            |
| Generator/setup/runtime/lock inputs or unknown root paths                     | Every affected generated configuration; cross-runtime inputs conservatively require all configurations                                 |
| Gate/check implementation                                                     | Representative presets and relevant fault detection/repair; Hook and lifecycle work have separate triggers                             |
| Hook/setup/process ownership                                                  | Real Linux/Windows Git event and cleanup rehearsals                                                                                    |
| Generator lifecycle/setup/startup ownership                                   | Cold/warm/cache-clear, HMR, addition, removal and recovery rehearsal once on generated Web                                             |
| Telemetry/Result policy, Collector/MCP profile or their shared inputs         | Source-free O11y integration; native producers on each actual OS when present                                                          |

Generated projects are prepared only for planned cases (`template:verify -- --cases web,api`, for example). Fault, Hook and lifecycle commands run directly on that prepared project; they do not regenerate and repeat its full gate first. The `required` summary always runs, requires success for every planned job and accepts a skipped job only when the plan explicitly marks it unnecessary. Workflow-level path filters would leave required checks pending, so selection happens inside the workflow. Security scanning remains independent, including its daily vulnerability refresh; an unrelated quality path cannot hide a HIGH/CRITICAL/ERROR finding.

Documentation exclusion is limited to explanatory text formats; code or configuration placed under `docs/` still receives its owning runtime or the conservative fallback. O11y selection covers producer/Result implementations and the actual Worker binding, Vite, runtime SDK and Cargo configuration inputs, so changing collection configuration cannot leave real signal checks unplanned.

Renderer-only generated checks explicitly use `env:setup -- --javascript`, `env:doctor -- --javascript` and the JavaScript gate scope. Their reports cannot satisfy native acceptance. A Desktop blueprint or native fault change still validates the generated Desktop on all three real OS, including when the source project itself is Web/API-only.

An explicit Quality `workflow_dispatch`, unavailable base or first checkout requests complete validation. Routine scoped CI and the full `acceptance:report` serve different purposes: the latter remains a strict complete template acceptance report and never relabels unexecuted full-suite evidence as passed. No test thresholds, assertions, OS requirements or security gates are relaxed by selection. Official [job conditions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-jobs-with-conditions) and [workflow triggers](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow) were checked on 2026-10-11.

Checks run sequentially to bound native/runtime memory; Vitest limits workers, and Vite+/Cargo own their task/build caches. The gate does not reuse previous successful reports. pnpm/Rust dependency caches accelerate warm execution without approving a different input. Reports in `artifacts/gate-*.json` include Git SHA/base, source content ID, OS/Node, selection, commands, timings and results. The gate rejects unexpected source changes; perform typegen/codegen with setup first.

CI retains root reports, package reports and package `test-results` on failure as well as success. Evidence archives preserve those project-relative directories, including Playwright's actual/difference screenshots and trace; a JSON attachment path alone does not preserve the referenced file.

The Playwright browser uses grayscale text antialiasing with Chromium's `--disable-lcd-text`, so host LCD subpixel preferences do not alter screenshot glyph edges. Existing reviewed baselines and zero differing-pixel allowance remain in force. This setting belongs to the browser regression environment; production application rendering and official Lighthouse browser profiles are unchanged.

Git hook installation is repo-local and repeatable. Existing `core.hooksPath` or active user hooks cause an explicit conflict; migrate them intentionally. Pre-commit validates a temporary exact index tree, links dependencies without pointing workspace imports at unstaged source, and never formats/restages/stashes. Its temporary tree has an isolated Git boundary and cleared repository-routing environment, so a project-local `TMPDIR` inside ignored `.state/` works without inheriting the parent ignore rules or modifying the original index/configuration. Real Git rehearsals use this ignored temporary location for valid, invalid and repaired commits, partial staging and linked worktrees. Pre-push checks detached copies of the actual pushed commits against each ref's remote SHA; it runs static/unit checks. Heavy build/runtime/native verification runs in the PR and final gate. The tiny shell Git adapters are the only Git-required shell entry; their work is Node TypeScript. No Agent-specific hook is advertised.

`pnpm template:verify` validates all selected generated configurations; `--faults --hooks --lifecycle` adds isolated fault, real Git event, HMR and lifecycle rehearsals. CI selects these mechanisms when their shared foundations change. Standalone `pnpm template:faults` also copies the selected project into an owned temporary directory; it never injects faults into the user checkout. Each fault must fail for the expected reason and pass after repair. CI runs this independently even if hooks were not used. Visual baselines are reviewed screenshots of the new sample; do not update them solely to silence a failure. Native E2E uses actual app/Rust IPC on the target OS; renderer units have separate names.

Unit fault probes temporarily replace a real tooling suite, restore its exact bytes and run that same suite successfully after every fault. The complete tooling suite runs once after all five unit repairs, preserving full coverage without repeating unrelated suites five times. Existing command and CI deadlines remain unchanged. Per-fault durations include detection, restoration and repair; use the whole CI step duration for total rehearsal time.

Normal project checks use `pnpm exec vp`. `verifyDepsBeforeRun: false` keeps script/exec entrypoints from silently installing dependencies; explicit setup and frozen installs own preparation. Missing dependencies still fail the doctor and mandatory checks. The exact staged snapshot invokes that same installed local Vite+ CLI directly to keep index validation read-only with its linked dependencies.

Use `pnpm acceptance:report -- --evidence <collected-artifacts-directory> --sha <generation-source-sha>` to derive the preset/OS/check/requirement matrix from the same preset registry and check definitions. Generated gates record source provenance, exact content, tool versions, commands, durations and build sizes. Missing, stale, failed, skipped or blocked required execution evidence produces a blocked report and a nonzero exit. Windows Worker CI evidence is mandatory alongside the native OS matrix; it must match the current clean source SHA, content ID, configuration and complete workspace/check graph. A Linux, dirty, narrowed or renderer report cannot satisfy it. Canonical workspace, checks and generation receipts are validated before choosing a baseline from mixed archives. Real Agent rehearsal reports are separately collected evidence; running a script never substitutes for an Agent. The report covers execution evidence; it does not grant merge approval or replace required GitHub checks and reviews. Report GitHub Template settings, protection/rules access, security audit findings and remote deployment separately when assessing all Issue conditions.

`node tools/quality/sanitize.ts --rules <external-rules.json>` scans source, dependency manifests, configuration, documentation and built bundles against task-specific extraction rules. Supply entries with `id`, `pattern` and optional exact-file `allow` entries with a reason. Product identifiers belong in that review input, never in general downstream lint policy. Legal/source-provenance exceptions must be explicit. Scanner errors report file/rule identifiers without printing matching secret text.

Hook, fault, lifecycle and template rehearsal reports include final owned-directory cleanup. They publish success only after cleanup; a cleanup failure replaces the report status with `failed` and propagates the error. Completed inner phases do not turn an unsuccessful wrapper into accepted mechanism evidence.

Disposable Hook, fault and lifecycle projects initialize their own empty Git boundary before setup. Caller-owned `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` may be inside a committed project's ignored directory; inherited Git routing is removed from foreign commands while the caller's index/configuration remain protected. Hook installation and linked cleanup discover their explicit project's Git metadata independently of exported routing. Owned-source SHA and dirty-state queries use the same cleared routing; ordinary `headSha` discovery retains its existing default behavior. Lifecycle server/native/database commands receive that owned environment. Changes to the shared `tools/quality/fixture.ts` and `checkout.ts` helpers select real Linux/Windows hooks and the Web lifecycle rehearsal; unrelated quality helpers retain their narrower selection.

[Security CI](security.md) additionally blocks HIGH/CRITICAL Trivy, ERROR Semgrep and incomplete scans. Its optional tools do not replace runtime gates. Never merge with an unresolved required security failure.

Type-aware lint rejects floating Promises even behind `void`, misused async callbacks and unhandled union cases; hooks, React keys, focused/disabled tests and explicit `any` also fail. [Failure contracts](errors.md) add Result/SDK ownership rules and catalog drift checks. The index hook runs structural lint; full quality runs types. Static JavaScript validation checks TypeScript/catalog documentation only; selected native checks additionally compare generated Rust and run Cargo formatting/Clippy. No Rust toolchain is needed for a Web/API project.

The required observability CI job runs a renamed/scoped generated fullstack project without the source checkout. It exercises real HTTP/browser CRUD, official read-only MCP and ClickHouse logs/traces/histograms; it validates failure and repaired trace IDs. When native work is planned, it requires current source SHA/content ID and save/cancel/error payload artifacts from each real Linux/macOS/Windows job, then verifies their actual Collector ingestion and correlation. Historical, renderer-only or fixture-generated payloads cannot satisfy this native condition.

The registry also owns `real-signals-mcp`: the optional Docker/MCP profile is verified once in CI using a separately named/scoped generated fullstack project without a source checkout. [Observability evidence](observability.md) requires actual ClickHouse logs, traces and histogram exemplars, readiness and bounded read-only MCP; if native is selected, all save/cancel/error producer artifacts from Linux/macOS/Windows must match the current source SHA/content ID and reach ClickHouse. `acceptance:report` requires this evidence alongside existing gates and rehearsals. Initialization failures replace old success with `not_run`/`failed`; source mutation and cleanup failures invalidate success.

# Template generation and updates

Version is recorded in the root manifest and `.template.json` with chosen preset/features, identity, package list and managed-file hashes. The blueprint directory is the sole sample source. Reference packages are derived; `pnpm template:sync` regenerates them and refuses conflicting edits. Project-local Vite+ supplies formatting; cold initialization uses only Node, and setup finalizes only unchanged managed files.

Initialization supports empty directories and a GitHub-template/reference clone. Defaults select web, not all dependencies. Supply `--name`, `--scope`, optional `--identifier`, `--preset web|api|desktop|fullstack|fullstack-desktop`, and `--features d1,kv,r2`. Fullstack always includes Service Bindings. `fullstack+desktop` is also accepted. `--dry-run` shows writes/removals without changing content; `--no-install` permits generation before tool preparation. Repeating the same identity/preset preserves downstream changes. A changed preset/identity requires clean managed files; ownership/path/case/symlink checks and a recovery journal protect user content.

`pnpm app:new -- --kind api --name jobs --features kv` adds an independent app and required shared packages. Root runtime selection reads manifests rather than a second dependency graph. It updates selected scripts and lock/install; it never rewrites other app sources. Unknown names/collisions fail. Prefer a service binding to an explicit API rather than implementation imports.

Cold additions without a complete project-local formatter invalidate the inherited formatting key. Standard setup then formats only unchanged managed scaffold files and refreshes their hashes; files edited by the user remain protected. A manifest without the formatter binary is an incomplete SDK, so it cannot mark generated files as already formatted.

Maintainer reference workspaces also record added applications' generation options in `.template.json` so `template:sync` can regenerate them from the same blueprints. This is reference generation metadata; generated projects continue to own their application code. The thin `packages/sample-api` reference service uses the API template without external storage bindings. Its package README gives the targeted development and deployment-preflight commands.

For upgrades, compare the recorded template version to the desired release, review blueprint/tool changes in a separate branch, apply infrastructure changes selectively, regenerate in an empty temporary directory and compare the diff. Protect downstream business code, migrations and licenses. No automatic downstream source overwrite, private registry or registry publication is part of this version.

The small Node renderer handles dependency-free preset selection and transactional ownership, which Vite+'s Bingo project generator does not provide directly for this repository. It delegates dev/build/check/test/format to the standard project-local tool rather than building another JS toolchain. Keep this comparison under review when upgrading Vite+.

`pnpm template:verify` uses owned temporary directories by default; `--output <directory>` retains each generated verification project. Each fresh verification project receives an empty, independent Git repository, without source history or user hook templates, so parent Git ignore rules and hook settings cannot affect checks. Existing nonempty verification destinations remain protected. A project initialized manually inside another Git repository must run `git init` at its own root before setup; setup refuses to change the parent Git configuration and doctor diagnoses this boundary.

To replace the sample, remove its routes/adapters and corresponding tests, add real tests for your own application, and update manifests to remove unused dependencies. Delete unused shared sample packages only after their consumers are changed. Runtime/generator/quality tools discover packages and test files through manifests/globs; they do not require the Notes implementation. Empty or skipped test suites fail rather than pretending the replacement is verified. `pnpm template:lifecycle` performs this replacement in an isolated project and actually installs, starts, checks, tests and builds it. It also measures cold/warm/cache-cleared gates, repeats initialization, protects user edits, changes identity/preset, adds an application and recovers an interrupted transaction.

Preset exclusion removes unchanged managed source and manifests, then prunes only their empty parent directories using nonrecursive removal. User files, ignored caches, unrelated empty directories and directories with setuid/setgid/sticky permission bits remain protected; only packages with valid manifests enter the workspace graph. Special permission bits are also checked immediately before removal to protect changes made after journaling. The existing version-1 transaction journal records ordinary directory paths/modes before removal, so interruption or a pruning error can restore missing parents before restoring files. Replacement and recovery preserve an existing file's ordinary permissions despite the process umask; new files honor that umask. Files with setuid/setgid/sticky bits require manual review before any transaction writes or removes them, and recovery refuses unsafe recorded modes. Adding a shared package verifies its identity, safely reuses cache-only directories, and refuses unowned source files.

Every preset includes portable contracts and observability, with no Docker/MCP installation implicit in ordinary setup. Error output is generated directly from the generated project's `tools/errors/catalog.json`, including when an API-only project later adds a differently named Desktop. There is no copied error-output blueprint to overwrite a customized catalog. Explicit `errors:generate` replaces derived output; setup finalizes only unchanged owned files.
